guidelines.detail: same as LRN-008 (The description says the team creates the content, designs the visuals and selects the channels, with no stated order, and the launch follows only after all of them. The reference places a parallel split before these activities and a parallel join before the launch (M4, M6). The generated model instead sequences them, which is a structural divergence. The reference's exclusive gateways (M2, M3) an)

The only semantic difference is that the reference models the campaign-period end as a task (M1), while the generated model uses an intermediate catch event (X1). The description (S5) describes a wait for a time-based condition, and BPMN 2.0.2 requires that to be an intermediate catch event, so the reference is the side that breaks semantics. The generator's choice is correct, not a mistake, so no new guideline should be derived from this difference. The remaining label pairs (P1, P2, P3, P8) are high-similarity wording variants with no structural difference, so they do not support a guideline

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names several activities that are carried out side by side, with no stated order among them, and a later step starts only after all of them are finished: Model a parallel split gateway before the group of activities, with one unconditional outgoing flow to each activity. Join the activities with a parallel join gateway, and connect one outgoing flow from that join to the later step. Do not add decision conditions to these branches, and do not chain the activities in sequence when the description does not order them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names several activities that are carried out side by side, with no stated order among them, and a later step starts only after all of them are finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the flow must wait until a stated period or deadline has elapsed before a later step or the end of the process
